title: Alchemy Profession
content: Alchemists turn herbs into potions, elixirs and flasks, so the profession pairs with Herbalism. Its Mixology perk makes the flasks and elixirs an alchemist knows stronger and longer-lasting on them, and transmutes turn materials into rarer ones, such as Titanium. Grand Master alchemy is taught in Dalaran.

expert_content: Transmute: Titanium has no cooldown, so run it whenever a Titanium Bar sells for more than the Saronite Bars it uses. Eternal transmutes share the daily transmute cooldown, so spend it on whichever Eternal sells highest. Pick Transmutation Master for procs on transmutes, or Elixir Master to proc extra flasks, and stock Flask of Endless Rage and Flask of the Frost Wyrm before raid nights.

title: Blacksmithing Profession
content: Blacksmiths make plate and mail armor, weapons and the Eternal Belt Buckle from bars smelted out of ore, so it pairs with Mining. Trainers are in most capitals, the Grand Master rank (skill 350 to 450) is taught in Dalaran, and at 400 skill a blacksmith can add a socket to their own bracers and gloves.

title: Enchanting Profession
content: Enchanters disenchant green and better items into dusts, essences and shards (Infinite Dust, Greater Cosmic Essence and Dream Shards in Northrend, Abyss Crystals from epics) and use them to enchant gear. It needs no gathering profession, and its perk is enchanting your own rings.

expert_content: Disenchant the cheap green and blue items other players list and sell the Infinite Dust, Greater Cosmic Essence and Dream Shards that come out, or use them yourself. Put popular enchants on a scribe's vellum and sell the scrolls: weapon enchants like Berserking and Black Magic and cloak and boot enchants move every day.

title: Engineering Profession
content: Engineers build guns, scopes, explosives and gadgets from mined metal, so it pairs with Mining. Their perk is tinkers only engineers can use, like Hyperspeed Accelerators on gloves and Nitro Boosts on boots, plus the Wormhole Generator: Northrend and the Mekgineer's Chopper or Mechano-Hog motorcycle.

title: Herbalism Profession
content: Herbalists gather herbs for Alchemy and Inscription, with Find Herbs showing nodes on the minimap. Northrend herbs include Goldclover, Tiger Lily, Adder's Tongue, Lichbloom, Icethorn and the rare Frost Lotus. The perk Lifeblood is a self-heal.

expert_content: Farm a loop in Sholazar Basin for Adder's Tongue, or Icecrown and the Storm Peaks for Lichbloom and Icethorn; any Northrend node can also give a Frost Lotus, which sells high. Herbs sell in stacks of 20 to scribes and alchemists.

title: Inscription Profession
content: Scribes mill herbs, five at a time, into pigments, turn those into inks, and make glyphs, off-hand books, Darkmoon Cards and vellums. Their perk is Master's Inscription shoulder enchants for themselves, and Grand Master Inscription is taught in Dalaran.

expert_content: Glyphs are the money: learn as many as you can through Northrend Inscription Research and Minor Inscription Research, mill the cheapest Northrend herbs for pigments, and list a few of every glyph so you are never out of stock. A finished Darkmoon Card deck, such as the one that makes Greatness, sells for a lot.

title: Jewelcrafting Profession
content: Jewelcrafters prospect ore, five at a time, for raw gems, cut them, and make rings, necklaces and trinkets, so it pairs with Mining. Their perk is Dragon's Eye gems only they can socket, up to three. Timothy Jones in Dalaran gives a daily quest paying tokens for new designs.

expert_content: Prospect Saronite and Titanium ore for gems; Titanium is the one that gives the epic gems. Cut what raiders actually socket, red strength, agility and spell power gems sell fastest, and do the Timothy Jones daily in Dalaran every day: its tokens buy new designs, Dragon's Eye designs included. Selling cut gems beats selling raw gems almost every time.

title: Leatherworking Profession
content: Leatherworkers make leather and mail armor, armor kits, leg armors like Icescale Leg Armor, and drums from skinned leather, so it pairs with Skinning. Their perk is Fur Lining bracer enchants for themselves.

title: Mining Profession
content: Mining is learned from a mining trainer in any capital or large town; a guard will point one out. Miners gather ore and stone from mineral nodes, shown on the minimap with Find Minerals, and smelt it into bars at a forge for Blacksmithing, Engineering and Jewelcrafting. Northrend ores are Cobalt, Saronite and the rare Titanium, and the perk Toughness adds stamina.

expert_content: Saronite is the volume ore, thickest in Sholazar Basin, Icecrown and the Storm Peaks, and a Saronite node can be a Titanium vein at random. Sell Titanium raw, or smelt it only when the bar is worth more than the ore. Mining plus Herbalism is the best pair for pure farming, since you pick up both nodes on one route.

title: Skinning Profession
content: Skinners skin dead beasts, and some dragonkin, for leather and hides used in Leatherworking; humanoids drop cloth instead. Northrend gives Borean Leather and the rare Arctic Fur, and the perk Master of Anatomy adds critical strike rating.

title: Tailoring Profession
content: Tailors sew cloth gear and bags from cloth looted off humanoids, like Frostweave Cloth in Northrend, and need no gathering profession. Their perk is cloak embroideries only they can use, Lightweave, Darkglow and Swordguard, and they make Moonshroud, Ebonweave and Spellweave cloth for the best tailored gear.

title: Cooking Profession
content: Cooking is a secondary profession anyone can learn alongside two primaries. Food gives Well Fed buffs, and the Fish Feast feeds a whole raid. Dozens of Northrend recipes are bought with Dalaran Cooking Awards from the cooking dailies of Katherine Lee or Awilo Lon'gomba in Dalaran.

title: Fishing Profession
content: Learn Fishing from a fishing trainer, buy a Fishing Pole, and cast in any open water; lures like Nightcrawlers add skill for ten minutes. Marcia Chase in Dalaran gives a daily fishing quest, and Stranglethorn Vale's Fishing Extravaganza runs on Sundays.

title: First Aid Profession
content: First Aid is a secondary profession every character can learn, used to make bandages from cloth that heal over a short channel. Damage interrupts a bandage, and Recently Bandaged blocks another for a minute. The best one, Dense Frostweave Bandage, is learned from a manual at 450 skill.

title: Professions
content: A character can have two primary professions, and most fill both: two gathering ones (Herbalism, Mining, Skinning) make the most gold, or one gathering plus the crafting one it feeds (Alchemy, Blacksmithing, Enchanting, Engineering, Inscription, Jewelcrafting, Leatherworking, Tailoring). Cooking, Fishing and First Aid are secondary and don't count. Skill caps at 450, taught by Grand Master trainers in Northrend.
